issues.description: The template's addGuestStudents method signature includes an extra boolean parameter (addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput)) which does not match the exercise specification and the solution implementation that expect a single int parameter (addGuestStudents(int)). This mismatch can confuse students about the required method signature and prevent them from following the specified API in the problem statement/UML and the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template method signature to match the specification and solution: change the method to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (remove the boolean parameter). If input validation is desired, implement it inside the single-parameter method or provide a separate overloaded/internal helper method so the public API matches the UML and exercise description.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution define an addGuestStudents method with a single int parameter (addGuestStudents(int): void), but the template declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). The extra boolean parameter in the template causes a signature mismatch so students cannot directly implement or call the method as specified in the exercise and tests, creating confusion and compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template method signature match the problem statement and solution by removing the extra boolean parameter. Change the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* ... */ } so that students and tests can use the single-parameter method described in the UML.
